senses.gloss: m. (preced.) [rugged,] Raʿats, the form of the Samaritan type, opp. אַשּׁוּרִית, q. v.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:4">Y. Meg. I, 71ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>בר׳ ניתנה התורה</he> the Torah was given in Raʿats characters.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:4">Ib.</cite> <he>אשורית … נהפך להן לר׳ וכ׳</he> the Torah was given them in Asshurith, but when they sinned, it was changed for them into Raʿats, and when they improved in Ezra’s days, it was changed &c.; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 22a:3">Snh. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>לרועץ</he> (Ms. F. <he>לרעוץ</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 200); <cite ref="Tosefta Sanhedrin 4:7">Tosef. ib. IV, 7</cite> <he>לרועץ</he>; Yalk. Ezra 1069 <he>לרועץ</he>.

Y. Meg. I, 71ᶜ top מאן דאמר בר׳ … עי״ן מעשה נסים (not לר׳) according to him who says that the Torah was given in R., the letter ʿAyin (Δ, cut out on the tablets of stone) was a work of miracle (there being no connection left with the body of the stone).—[Ar. quotes a Var. דַּעַץ wedge-like.]
